g.title: G
cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag intra_scale A new exposure transition can later manifest as infectiousness without diagnosis, raising the chance the agent enters the silent-infectious state after the biological delay.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag intra_scale Agents newly exposed can progress to symptomatic disease before being diagnosed, so exposure transitions feed later symptomatic-undiagnosed states.
p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale A newly observed exposure may be recorded through source investigation and thereby raise the agent's known-contact flag.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale If an exposure event is linked to a traced source or known contact investigation, the newly exposed agent may be placed under quarantine.

p1_micro_new_exposure_flag → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale The timing of the exposure transition sets the start of the exposure-to-diagnosis interval and can shift when diagnosis eventually occurs.

p1_micro_ever_exposed_state → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Previously exposed agents plausibly share exposure settings with recognized cases, making them more likely to be flagged as known contacts in later tracing rounds.

p1_micro_ever_exposed_state → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale An agent with prior exposure may be more readily quarantined when contact tracing or clinical recognition identifies a plausible infection link.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale Agents with more incident edges in a layer have more opportunities for exposure transitions attributed to that layer, so per-layer degree can raise the likelihood of a layer-attributed exposure event.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Higher contact degree increases the chance that an agent is identified as a known contact after a diagnosis, because more contact links are available for tracing.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Agents with more contacts are more likely to be quarantined when tracing capacity reaches their contact neighborhood, linking degree to quarantine status.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta intra_scale A higher pre-quarantine contact degree can make the drop in contacts during quarantine larger, shifting the within-agent degree delta downward.

p2_micro_layer_degree → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough intra_scale High-degree agents are likely to be exposed earlier in the epidemic wave, which can move their first observed exposure step relative to the city infectious trough.

p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag intra_scale Exposure attributed to a contact layer can lead to infection that remains undiagnosed, later producing silent infectious activity.

p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag intra_scale Layer-specific exposure can produce symptomatic infection that is not yet diagnosed, linking setting-attributed exposure to later undiagnosed symptoms.

p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale When exposure is attributed to a traced layer, the exposed agent is more likely to be flagged as a known contact in that setting.
p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Layer-attributed exposure can trigger contact tracing and subsequent quarantine of the exposed agent.

p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag intra_scale Exposure attributed to a contact layer may lead to quarantine and full contact suppression, making zero-contact quarantined states more likely.

p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale The contact setting of exposure can affect how quickly infection is recognised and diagnosed, shifting the exposure-to-diagnosis interval.
p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag intra_scale Higher cumulative contact weight in a layer plausibly raises the chance that an agent experiences a new exposure transition.
p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale A larger per-layer weight load can make exposures more likely to be attributed to that same contact layer.

p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag intra_scale When the high-load layer is the persistent household-like setting, greater contact weight plausibly increases household-attributed exposures.

p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Higher contact weight load raises infection risk and can indirectly increase the chance of later quarantine through detection or tracing.
p2_micro_layer_beta_load → p7_micro_exposure_step_index intra_scale Agents with larger contact weight loads are plausibly exposed earlier, shifting their first observed exposure step downward.

p3_micro_household_degree → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag intra_scale More household-layer contacts increase the chance that an exposure transition has a recorded source within the persistent household-like layer.
p3_micro_household_degree → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Household contacts of an index case are plausible tracing targets, so greater household degree can raise known-contact flagging.
p3_micro_household_degree → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale More household contacts imply more opportunities to be placed under quarantine as a contact of a diagnosed household member.

p3_micro_household_degree → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta intra_scale High household degree can make quarantine reduce total contacts less if household contacts persist, altering the degree delta under quarantine.

p3_micro_household_degree → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough intra_scale Household contact structure can sustain exposure into later phases, shifting first exposure steps relative to the infectious trough.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag intra_scale Source-attributed exposure represents a traceable infection event that can later become silent infectious activity if diagnosis is delayed.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag intra_scale An exposure with a recorded source can progress to symptomatic but still undiagnosed infection, linking attribution to later undiagnosed symptoms.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Source-attributed exposures are more readily entered into contact tracing, raising the chance the agent is flagged as a known contact.
p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Knowing the source of an exposure can prompt quarantine of the exposed agent, increasing quarantine-state occurrence.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag intra_scale A source-attributed exposure may lead to quarantine and stronger activity reduction, making full contact suppression more likely.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale Traceable exposure events can shorten the time to diagnosis through follow-up, changing the exposure-to-diagnosis interval.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag intra_scale An agent exposed within the household may later progress to symptomatic but still undiagnosed infection before care is sought.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale A household-attributed exposure plausibly marks the agent as a contact of a household case, increasing known-contact flagging.
p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Household exposure is a plausible trigger for quarantine after a household case is recognized.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag intra_scale A silently infectious agent can generate new exposure transitions among contacts without being diagnosed, increasing undetected exposure activity.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Undiagnosed silent infectiousness makes it less likely that the agent's contacts are recognized and flagged, weakening known-contact signaling.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Silent infectious agents are less visible to surveillance, so they are less likely to be quarantined through diagnosis-driven pathways.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale When infectiousness remains silent, the recorded interval from exposure to eventual diagnosis can lengthen because diagnosis is delayed.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough intra_scale Silent infectious activity can sustain exposures after a visible decline, shifting first exposure steps to later positions relative to the trough.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Longer silent infectious duration delays case detection and contact elicitation, tending to reduce known-contact flagging among contacts.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p5_micro_tracing_latency intra_scale Prolonged undiagnosed infectious activity can delay the index case being recognised, lengthening known-contact-to-quarantine latency.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Longer silent infectious duration implies later detection and therefore fewer opportunities for timely quarantine of associated contacts.

p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale Silent infectious activity that persists longer tends to lengthen the interval between exposure and eventual diagnosis.

p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration intra_scale Undiagnosed symptomatic infection plausibly extends the time an agent remains silently infectious because recognition is delayed.
p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p5_micro_tracing_latency intra_scale Symptomatic but undiagnosed agents plausibly experience longer delays before their contacts are identified and traced.
p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale Undiagnosed symptoms can lengthen the interval between exposure and eventual diagnosis.

p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag intra_scale Agents with symptomatic undiagnosed infection after the city trough plausibly continue generating post-trough exposure events.
p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_micro_tracing_latency intra_scale Being flagged as a known contact starts the tracing process, and the timing of that flag shapes the observed latency to quarantine.
p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale A known-contact flag can directly lead to quarantine once tracing completes, increasing quarantine-state occurrence.

p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio intra_scale Known-contact flagging often precedes quarantine, and the resulting change in contact degree shapes the quarantined-to-nonquarantined contact ratio.
p5_micro_known_contact_flag → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag intra_scale Known-contact tracing can place agents under quarantine, where adherence may produce full contact suppression.
p5_micro_tracing_latency → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Longer known-contact-to-quarantine latency plausibly delays quarantine onset for the affected agent.

p5_micro_tracing_latency → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio intra_scale Slower tracing allows more contact activity before quarantine, plausibly altering the ratio of in-quarantine to out-of-quarantine degree.
p5_micro_tracing_latency → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta intra_scale Longer tracing latency can reduce the observed drop in contact degree once quarantine begins, changing the degree delta.
p5_micro_tracing_latency → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag intra_scale Slow tracing after the trough plausibly leaves more exposure events occurring after the city infectious minimum.

p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio intra_scale Quarantine status changes an agent's contact opportunities, so the in- versus out-of-quarantine degree ratio is shaped by when and whether the agent is quarantined.
p5_micro_quarantine_flag → p7_micro_exposure_step_index intra_scale Being quarantined before exposure reduces contact opportunities and can delay an agent's first observed exposure step.

p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale An agent's residual contact while quarantined may influence whether isolation is maintained or renewed, feeding back into observed quarantine state.
p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p7_micro_exposure_step_index intra_scale A higher residual contact ratio increases exposure opportunity, tending to make first exposure occur earlier.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale A larger contact reduction under quarantine lowers subsequent layer-specific exposure opportunities, reducing layer-attributed exposure transitions.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag intra_scale If quarantine suppresses non-household contacts more than household contacts, remaining exposures are more likely to be household-attributed.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale Stronger contact reduction after quarantine can lower further contact-tracing signals by cutting the effective contact neighborhood.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough intra_scale Behavioral suppression during quarantine can delay exposure events and shift their timing relative to the city infectious trough.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag intra_scale Full contact suppression during quarantine removes exposure opportunities, reducing subsequent new-exposure transitions for that agent.

p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale Quarantined agents with zero recorded contacts cannot acquire layer-attributed exposures, lowering later layer exposure events.
p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Earlier exposure can lead to earlier isolation or quarantine status in later sampled steps, shifting the agent's quarantine flag.

p7_micro_exposure_step_index → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio intra_scale Exposure timing determines when an agent enters quarantine, changing the mix of quarantined and non-quarantined steps over which the contact ratio is averaged.
p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag intra_scale Longer diagnostic delay increases the chance that an agent is observed as infectious while still undiagnosed.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration intra_scale A longer exposure-to-diagnosis interval creates more opportunity for infectious person-steps before diagnosis, extending silent infectious duration.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p5_micro_known_contact_flag intra_scale A longer interval between exposure and diagnosis can weaken timely contact identification, reducing known-contact flagging.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p5_micro_tracing_latency intra_scale Delayed diagnosis after exposure can propagate into longer known-contact-to-quarantine latency because tracing starts later.

p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough intra_scale Cohorts with different exposure-to-diagnosis intervals can shift which exposure steps are observed near the trough.

p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag intra_scale Exposures occurring later relative to the trough may take place under changed contact restrictions, altering the layer attribution of exposure transitions.

p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag intra_scale Post-trough exposures can become more household-centered if community contacts remain reduced, increasing household-attributed exposure probability.

p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta intra_scale Later exposure relative to the trough may coincide with weaker quarantine adherence, making the quarantine degree delta less negative.

p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough → p7_micro_exposure_to_diagnosis_interval intra_scale Exposure timing relative to the trough can change surveillance and care-seeking conditions, affecting the recorded exposure-to-diagnosis interval.

p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag intra_scale Post-trough exposures can seed new infections that remain undiagnosed, contributing to silent infectious activity during resurgence.
p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag intra_scale Exposure events after the infectious trough can produce symptomatic but undiagnosed cases as resurgence unfolds.
p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag → p5_micro_quarantine_flag intra_scale Post-trough exposure may prompt renewed tracing and quarantine, increasing quarantine-state occurrence among exposed agents.

p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Age bands with high hazard may concentrate exposure activity in particular settings, raising per-edge incidence in those layers.
p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count intra_scale Age bands with high hazard may include household members who generate more secondary exposures within household dyads.

p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p4_meso_group_silent_share intra_scale Age-band hazard affects who becomes infected, and age-specific diagnosis and quarantine can change the silent share within quarantine-status groups.

p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p7_meso_band_share_drift intra_scale A higher exposure hazard in an age band can raise that band's share of new exposures, producing drift in band composition over time.

p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale A band's pre-trough hazard shapes its depletion and remaining susceptible pool, affecting its post-trough incidence ratio.

p1_meso_band_attack_ratio → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale A higher cumulative attack ratio in an age band depletes susceptible members and can lower the band's subsequent exposure hazard per susceptible person-step.

p1_meso_band_attack_ratio → p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion intra_scale Unequal cumulative attack across bands can widen or narrow cross-band hazard dispersion as susceptible depletion differs by band.

p1_meso_band_attack_ratio → p4_meso_group_silent_share intra_scale Heavily affected age bands can contribute disproportionately to undiagnosed infectious person-steps, shifting the silent share in quarantine-status groups.

p1_meso_band_attack_ratio → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Higher band attack ratios generate more diagnosed cases and tracing demand, which can raise layer-level known-contact incidence per edge.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p1_meso_band_attack_ratio intra_scale Unequal exposure hazard across age bands can generate divergent cumulative attack ratios, with high-hazard bands accumulating more infections.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent intra_scale When hazard is concentrated in certain bands, exposures generated per silent infectious person-step can rise in the groups where those bands are active.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p7_meso_band_exposure_share intra_scale Dispersion of band-specific exposure hazard shifts the composition of new exposure transitions toward bands with higher hazard.
p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p7_meso_band_share_drift intra_scale Changing cross-band hazard dispersion can move band exposure shares away from their initial composition, producing share drift.
p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale High per-edge incidence in a layer drives exposure among agents active there, raising band-specific exposure hazard.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count intra_scale Higher per-edge incidence in the persistent household-like layer can raise expected secondary exposure counts in specific dyads.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p4_meso_group_silent_share intra_scale Higher per-edge incidence in a layer can generate more undiagnosed infections, increasing the silent share among groups active there.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale Higher incidence per edge in a layer can prompt stronger quarantine adherence or control, increasing the observed degree suppression ratio.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Concentration of layer degree among few agents can raise exposure incidence per edge by concentrating contact opportunities.
p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_meso_layer_active_run intra_scale Highly uneven layer degree can sustain repeated attributed exposures in a layer by repeatedly involving high-degree agents.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale When layer degree is concentrated, newly quarantined index agents may carry more layer-specific edges, increasing per-index contact load.
p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion intra_scale Degree dispersion across agents can propagate into cross-layer dispersion of tracing contact load.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale A layer that has been active for consecutive steps may accumulate susceptible depletion, changing the per-edge incidence rate in that setting.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Sustained activity in a layer generates more opportunities for contact elicitation, raising known-contact transitions per edge in that layer.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale Layer persistence can increase the number of in-layer contacts attached to newly quarantined index agents, raising per-index contact load.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share intra_scale A layer with a longer active run contributes more attributed exposure transitions, increasing its share of setting-level incident activity.
p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale Household dyad secondary exposures contribute to age-band-specific exposure incidence, raising band hazard.
p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Concentrated dyad-level secondary transmission can contribute to overall per-edge incidence in that layer.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale Concentrated secondary exposures in household dyads can trigger quarantine and stronger contact reduction in that layer.
p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p1_meso_band_attack_ratio intra_scale Household dyad concentration can alter age-band attack ratios because household structures differ across age groups.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction intra_scale Concentration of attributed exposures in few household dyads can reduce the fraction of dyads with any attributed exposure by leaving many dyads unaffected.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent intra_scale Highly dispersed household dyad exposures can change silent exposure yield by spreading infection activity across quarantine-status groups.

p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion intra_scale A higher fraction of dyads with attributed exposure can coincide with more uneven accumulation across dyads, raising dispersion of dyad counts.

p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Household-like dyad attack concentration can sustain later within-dyad transmission and lift post-trough incidence in that layer.
p4_meso_group_silent_share → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale A higher silent infectious share in groups can increase undetected exposure pressure, raising age-band exposure hazard.
p4_meso_group_silent_share → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Silent infectious agents remaining active in contact layers can contribute exposure events per edge, raising layer incidence.

p4_meso_group_silent_share → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count intra_scale Silent infectious household members can transmit without being diagnosed, raising attributed secondary exposure counts within household dyads.

p4_meso_group_silent_share → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale A high silent share can weaken the apparent need for quarantine and reduce observed suppression in layers those groups use.

p4_meso_group_silent_share → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Silent infectious activity can seed renewed transmission in age bands after the trough, raising post-trough band incidence ratios.
p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale Silent exposure yield in a group can feed age-band exposure hazards when group membership overlaps with age bands.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale High silent exposure yield can raise layer-level incidence per contact edge by generating undetected exposure transitions in contact settings.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p4_meso_group_silent_share intra_scale Groups that generate more exposures per silent infectious person-step can sustain a larger silent share of infectious person-steps.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Silent exposure generation can increase later known-contact transitions when contacts are eventually traced, affecting layer-level tracing yield.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale More effective layer-level known-contact detection can reduce subsequent exposure incidence per edge by interrupting transmission chains.
p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale A higher known-contact rate per layer edge implies more tracing follow-up per edge, raising per-index contact load.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Index agents with higher in-layer contact load create more opportunities for onward exposure, raising layer incidence per edge.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale High per-index contact load can strain tracing capacity, reducing known-contact transitions completed per edge in the layer.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Uneven tracing load across layers plausibly lowers known-contact yield in overloaded layers relative to less burdened settings.
p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale Dispersion in layer load reflects high-burden layers where each index plausibly requires more contact work.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale Overloaded tracing layers may produce weaker quarantine follow-through, plausibly reducing observable degree suppression there.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share intra_scale Tracing burden concentrated in some layers can shift where exposures are detected and attributed, changing layer exposure shares.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Layers with persistently high tracing load may be less suppressed after the trough, plausibly raising their post-trough incidence ratio.
p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load intra_scale Wide variation in quarantined degree changes how many contacts must be examined per index in affected layers.

p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale Heterogeneous contact behavior among quarantined agents plausibly weakens layer-level suppression because some retain many contacts.
p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share intra_scale Heterogeneous adherence can shift exposure activity toward layers where quarantined agents retain more contacts.

p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Residual contacts among less compliant quarantined agents plausibly drive layer-specific activity after the trough.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale Greater degree suppression among quarantined agents reduces contact and transmission per edge, lowering layer incidence.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count intra_scale Stronger quarantine suppression in a layer reduces contact opportunities, lowering attributed secondary exposures within household dyads.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p4_meso_group_silent_share intra_scale Stronger quarantine suppression in a layer can reduce silent transmission among active group members, lowering the silent share.
p7_meso_band_exposure_share → p1_meso_band_attack_ratio intra_scale A larger share of new exposures falling in a band can drive that band's cumulative attack ratio upward over subsequent steps.

p7_meso_band_exposure_share → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Bands with larger exposure shares can sustain relatively higher post-trough exposure rates, shaping age-specific resurgence ratios.
p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale If layers differ by age composition, shifting exposure shares across layers can plausibly alter age-band exposure hazards.
p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale A layer capturing more exposure transitions can plausibly show higher attributed incidence per recorded edge.
p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate intra_scale Settings contributing more exposures plausibly generate more known-contact transitions per contact edge.
p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Layers with larger exposure shares before or at the trough may be more likely to sustain post-trough incidence.
p7_meso_band_share_drift → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard intra_scale Shifts in a band's share of exposure events can change its susceptible and contact mix, altering its later exposure hazard.

p7_meso_band_share_drift → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio intra_scale Changing age composition of exposures can shift which bands carry infection into the post-trough period, altering their post-trough ratios.
p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge intra_scale A layer with elevated post-trough incidence plausibly contributes to later per-edge incidence in that setting.
